_comment: Labeled detection corpus (H9). Each case is realistic generated prose. `expect` maps a character name → the genome it SHOULD propose (empty = no species proposal for that character). `must` = genomes that must appear somewhere; `mustNot` = genomes that must NOT appear anywhere. `note` explains the hard part. Used by tools/detect-eval.ts for precision/recall.

cases.text: Something huge lunges from the dark. Teeth sink into her shoulder, and a low growl fills the night.
cases.note: implied werewolf: bite + growl, no species word

cases.text: Mira stumbles back as a wolf bursts from the trees.
cases.note: named species in a named clause

cases.text: Mira's skin prickles as fur spreads like a fox, while Tomas hunches, growing eagle wings.
cases.note: two characters, two species, clause attribution

cases.text: Ada is quick as a fox, darting between the stalls.
cases.note: simile 'as a fox' — still a fox, but a weak signal

cases.text: Fur ripples along her arms. Her ears sharpen and slide up her skull, and a muzzle pushes out her jaw.
Scales erupt along his forearms, cool and bright, and his tongue flicks out forked.
Bo was always a bear of a man, broad and warm.
A wolfish grin spread across her face.
Her nails lengthen into curving claws and her eyes flash amber.
Pat pours coffee and reads the paper on a grey morning.
It was not a wolf at her door, but something older.
It was no ordinary dog — this thing had a wolf's hunger.
No fur, no fangs — Sam looked entirely herself this morning.
cases.note: negated anatomy; must not imply a canine

cases.text: Sam is human, through and through — no fur, no fangs.
cases.note: explicitly human, anatomy named as absent

cases.text: The moon was full and Dee threw back her head and howled.
Fangs pierced her neck and the world went cold as he drank.
Wings burst from Tomas's back, wide and feathered.
Sarah stumbles back as a wolf lunges.
cases.note: first half of a two-message test

prior: A wolf lunges from the undergrowth and Sarah stumbles back.
cases.text: She screams as it bites her arm.
cases.note: bare pronominal follow-up keeps the focus

cases.text: Xen, a wolf with a nice ass, trotted over.
Nell swung up onto the horse and rode for the ridge.
cases.note: riding a horse is not becoming one — acceptable either way, but must not be dog

cases.text: Her pupils narrowed to slits and she stretched, feline and slow.
Zee's skin hardened into scales and heat rolled off her in waves.
cases.note: scales + heat, anatomy/hint-level reptile (serpent is the reptilian rep)
